newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHEARER REFUSES TO DWELL ON POIGNANT PAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHEARER REFUSES TO DWELL ON POIGNANT PAST.

text.p: Alan Shearer will not be weighed down by nostalgia when he returns to Blackburn on Thursday for the first time since his world record 15 million pounds ($23.3 million) move to Newcastle.
Shearer has fond memories of his four years at Blackburn but the England skipper now has his sights firmly fixed on chasing honours with his hometown club.

"In football, you can't look back," said Shearer. "I had four tremendous years there. I won a trophy, scored a lot of goals, and made a lot of friends, but I've got the move I always wanted so I'm looking to the future now."
Newcastle will be able to enter 1997 with renewed confidence if they can shrug off the faltering form that has seen them go six English league games without a win.
Shearer believes there were encouraging signs in Monday's 1-1 draw at home to leaders Liverpool -- a result which left Newcastle seven points adrift of the pacemakers.
"We're expecting a really tough one against Blackburn, but our second-half performance against Liverpool has given us something to build on," added Shearer. "It was our best performance for a while."
Shearer can expect a warm reception from Blackburn fans, but he has been warned not to expect any favours by Colin Hendry.

Blackburn's Scotland defender, who will have the job of preventing Shearer making a scoring return, said: "I think the general response of the supporters will be one of nice to see you again Alan'. But that will be before the game, once it kicks off he will become just another opposing player."
Liverpool will try to continue their recent free-scoring home form after Middlesbrough (5-1) and Nottingham Forest (4-2) felt the force of their attack in the last two games at Anfield.

Their injury-hit opponents Leicester are missing the influence of inspirational skipper Steve Walsh, but manager Martin O'Neill will be hoping his team can bounce back from their disappointing 2-0 home defeat by Coventry.
Second-placed Arsenal, three points behind Liverpool with a game in hand, have skipper Tony Adams back in central defence after suspension for their match at Sheffield Wednesday.
Lee Dixon will return at right-back in place of Gavin McGowan if he is passed fit, while Reme Garde is expected to continue to deputise for his suspended fellow Frenchman Patrick Vieira in midfield.

Nottingham Forest caretaker player-manager Stuart Pearce's only real selection poser for the visit of defending champions Manchester United is whether on-loan Nigel Clough should be in the starting line-up.

Dutchman Bryan Roy's place is under threat from midfielder Clough as Pearce seeks to consolidate in his new role after bottom club Forest beat Arsenal 2-1 last Saturday in his first game in charge following Frank Clark's resignation.

United defender Gary Pallister is expected to be missing with a back injury while England midfielder David Beckham, who has sat out the last two games, may be on the bench again following the 5-0 demolition of Sunderland last weekend.
